text:
Miguel Rivera: Heads-up — ACME hit ~72% of their monthly committed credits after a burst of embedding jobs this morning. Noticed lots of long prompts from Search API.
Tara Chen: Ack. Any idea if this is a single service spike or multiple teams? :eyes:
Miguel Rivera: Looks like two jobs: nightly ingestion + a new 'related-docs' batch they rolled out last night. Sam can share numbers.
Sam Patel: Quick numbers: last 12h tokens = 18.2M, typical daily = 7.5M. If trend continues projected month usage = ~540M tokens vs commit 700M => still safe but daily burnup shows a 7-day runway at current pace for on-demand. Spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcDE-example (QBR tab).
Jess Ortega: Onboarding note — we enabled prefix caching for them but ttl was 0. Need to push a config to 24h to cut repeated generator calls. That alone should reduce token load by ~15%.
Emily Ng: Good catch Jess. Can you add the TTL change to the runbook? I'll propose an enablement item in the QBR: caching + recommended prompt trims.
Miguel Rivera: Also recommend we enable cheap-embedding model fallback for bulk indexing jobs. Can we set a routing policy?
Sam Patel: Proposed routing rule (draft):
```
if request.type == \"bulk_embedding\" and request.size > 1000:
  route_to: ada-emb-lite
  max_batch: 2048
  fallback: rw-emb-std
```
That saves ~60%/token for bulk jobs.
Tara Chen: Nice. Can finance-bot run a 30/60/90 spend forecast after applying TTL + routing changes? Need that for the QBR deck.
finance-bot: Automated forecast queued. Running estimated-savings simulation with toggles: {\"prefix_ttl\":24h, \"emb_fallback\":true}. ETA 12m.
Miguel Rivera: Also flag renewal risk — if they keep experimenting without guidance they could overshoot next invoice cycle. Recommend we set an alert at 85% of commit and a pre-alert to CSM at 70%.
Sam Patel: Alert rule we can add to monitoring: 
```
alert_name: commit_usage_prealert
expression: (usage_last_24h / commit_total) > 0.7
notify: #cs-ops, @Emily Ng
severity: info
```
and final_alert at 0.85 -> pager to oncall + finance.
Jess Ortega: I'll include a one-pager in the QBR slides: \"Immediate fixes (TTL + cheap-emb) + next steps (prompt minimization, scheduled audits)\". Short bullets so execs can act.
Emily Ng: Schedule the pre-QBR sync for Friday 10am PT. I'll invite ACME CSM + solutions engineer. Also add cost scenarios (baseline, optimistic, post-ops).
Tara Chen: Perfect. After finance-bot finishes the sim, drop the numbers into the QBR tab and I'll craft the renewal risk slide.
finance-bot: Simulation complete. Results: baseline projection = 520M tokens, with TTL + emb_fallback = 440M tokens (~15.4% reduction). Estimated monthly spend change: -$1,200 (approx). Updated sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1aBcDE-example#gid=218
Miguel Rivera: :thumbsup: Can we also add a small snippet for the customer support playbook so CSMs can quickly toggle caching or request routing? Something like a CLI snippet or UI path.
Sam Patel: CLI example for ops team: 
```
redwood routes update acme --rule \"bulk_embedding\" --route ada-emb-lite --priority 50
redwood cache set acme --prefix-ttl 24h
```
Drop that in the playbook.
Emily Ng: Thanks team — I'll own the QBR slide deck and host the Friday sync. Jess, can you draft the playbook and share by Thursday EOD?
Jess Ortega: On it. Will post draft in this thread when ready.
Tara Chen: I'll prep talking points for the renewal risk slide. Miguel — please add any technical risks you want called out.
Miguel Rivera: Adding: potential token spikes from A/B tests; recommend gating experiments with a feature flag that has a token budget.
Emily Ng: Noted. Meeting invite sent. Closing action list: Jess=playbook, Sam=insert CLI + numbers in sheet, Tara=slide draft, Miguel=flag recommendations, finance-bot=attach final numbers to QBR doc.
finance-bot: Attached forecast CSV to thread: https://storage.redwood.ai/forecasts/acme-march-forecast.csv
Tara Chen: Thanks — seeing the CSV. Will finalize slides after reviewing. :white_check_mark:
